program.name: Swift Agent — Core Runtime Completion
program.description: Complete and harden the SDK registration-to-model-to-remote-tool-to-response execution path across REST and WebSocket entry points.

successCriteria.description: SDK registration persists the normalized name, description, and input schema for every declared tool without persisting execution handlers.
Existing agents without persisted tools remain readable and behave as agents with an empty tool list.
OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google provider requests receive the registered tool definitions on every applicable model turn.
A model-emitted tool call is rejected before execution when its name is not registered or its input does not satisfy the persisted schema.
Provider-native call identifiers round-trip correctly while every persisted tool call uses a Swift Agent tc_ identifier.
A registered tool call is persisted, executed by the active agent's remote SDK runner, returned to the model, and followed by a final assistant response.
Two agents with different runner configurations use their respective executors without cross-routing.
Runner requests use short-lived scoped authentication and reject unauthorized, expired, or scope-mismatched calls.
Deployed remote execution rejects disallowed outbound targets and enforces request, response, and deadline limits.
A retried remote invocation cannot execute the same logical tool call more than once when transport replay protection is enabled.
REST run creation returns 202, executes without a WebSocket client, and remains observable through run, message, tool-call, and trace endpoints.
REST and WebSocket entry points create one run and exhibit the same persistence and terminal-state behavior.
Repeated cancellation requests are safe, and a cancelled run cannot later transition to completed, failed, or timed out.
Model, tool, and total-run deadlines abort supported work and persist timed_out state.
Provider, validation, transport, and tool-handler failures finalize run, tool-call, and trace records consistently.
Integration tests cover successful no-tool runs, successful remote-tool runs, multiple tool turns, cancellation, timeout, replay, SSRF rejection, and each defined failure boundary.
Monorepo type-checking, linting, unit tests, and runtime integration tests pass.
